# Local documentation packs for the AI tutor

Two downloadable archives give the Zed AI tutor (the `Ask` and `Write` profiles) a
local, searchable copy of everything it needs to teach this course. The tutor
reads the files with `read_file` and `grep` — no network `fetch`, no external site,
and the material stays under your control.

- **llm-project.zip** — the previous course, re-edited as LLM-friendly markdown
  (47 `.llms.md` files).
- **python-doc.zip** — the official Python 3.12 library reference for the modules
  the course uses, converted to markdown.

Download, unzip where you keep your working files, then tell the tutor where the
folder is (or point it there in its instructions). Each archive keeps its
top-level folder, so the two unpack cleanly side by side.

## llm-project.zip — the previous course, LLM-ready

The 2024–2025 course on advanced programming and parallel computing, re-edited as
standalone markdown chapters small enough to read or search in one pass.

```text
llm-project/
├── llms.txt            # index of the whole pack
├── courses/
│   ├── Courses/        # 12 chapters (code assistant, async, IPC, distributed, SIMD, GPU, WebGPU…)
│   └── Projects/
├── applications/       # 14 worked applications (prompt engineering, numpy, async, IPC, numba…)
└── solutions/          # 14 exercise solutions
```

Download: [llm-project.zip](downloads/llm-project.zip)

Use it to look up how a notion was taught before, reuse an application as an
example, or hand the tutor a concrete course reference instead of a generic
explanation.

## python-doc.zip — official Python 3.12 library docs

The official CPython library reference for the modules the course relies on,
converted to markdown. `README.md` in the archive maps each module to its course
chapter:

| Files | Content | Course chapter(s) |
|---|---|---|
| `asyncio` (5 files) | event loops, tasks, streams, primitives, subprocess | `01_asynchronous` |
| `concurrent.futures` | thread/process pools | `00_intro-parallelism`, `01_asynchronous` |
| `threading` | threads, locks | `00_intro-parallelism`, `02_ipc-locks` |
| `multiprocessing` | processes, pipes, queues, managers, locks | `02_ipc-locks`, `03_distributed` |
| `multiprocessing.shared_memory` | shared memory | `02_ipc-locks`, `03_distributed` |
| `queue` | thread-safe queues | `00_intro-parallelism`, `02_ipc-locks` |
| `socket` | sockets | `02_ipc-locks`, `03_distributed` |
| `subprocess` | subprocesses | `00_intro-parallelism`, `02_ipc-locks` |

Download: [python-doc.zip](downloads/python-doc.zip)

The archive keeps `fetch_docs.py`, which regenerates the markdown from the CPython
**3.12** sources (pinned branch, needs `pandoc`), so the text matches the Python
that runs on the course machines.

A documented limit: the SIMD, GPU, and WebGPU chapters (`04_simd`, `05_gpu`,
`06_webgpu`) rely on libraries outside the standard library — NumPy, Numba, CuPy,
WebGPU. Their documentation is not included here; `README.md` lists the official
links if a tutoring session needs them.

Derived from the official
[Python 3.12 documentation](https://docs.python.org/3.12/library/), under the
Python Software Foundation License. The `llm-project` pack is the previous
year's teaching material, provided as-is for reference.
